events.title: Cuba's Ten Years' War Begins
events.description: On this day, Cuban landowner Carlos Manuel de Céspedes issued a call for independence from Spain. That began the first major armed struggle for Cuban freedom, known as the Ten Years' War.
events.significance: The long conflict ended without independence. It still laid the foundation for the later independence movement and became a defining part of Cuban national identity.

events.title: The Wuchang Uprising
events.description: A day after a bomb went off by accident and exposed their plans, revolutionary soldiers in Wuchang rose up against the Qing dynasty. The revolt quickly spread to other provinces.
events.significance: The uprising led to the fall of China's imperial system and the founding of the Republic of China. October 10 is still celebrated in Taiwan as National Day, often called Double Ten.

events.title: Panama Canal's Last Barrier Destroyed
events.description: President Woodrow Wilson sent a telegraph signal from the White House. It set off an explosion that destroyed the Gamboa Dike and let water flow through the Culebra Cut.
events.significance: The blast joined the Atlantic and Pacific waters across the canal route. The canal opened to ships in 1914 and transformed global maritime trade.

events.title: Tokyo Olympics Open
events.description: The Summer Olympic Games opened in Tokyo. They were the first Olympics held in Asia.
events.significance: The Games showed the world Japan's remarkable postwar recovery. They also marked a new era of global broadcasting and modern Olympic organization.
